source.title: Evaluating reproducibility of AI algorithms in digital pathology with DAPPER
source.authors: A. Bizzego; Nicole Bussola; M. Chierici; V. Maggio; Margherita Francescatto; Luca Cima; M. Cristoforetti; Giuseppe Jurman; Cesare Furlanello

page_placements.theme: Randomized-label controls reveal evaluation dependence and leakage

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study runs a random-label diagnostic with a DAP and reports MCC, but it trains classifiers on frozen deep features rather than testing whether the full networks fit random labels as in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study's random-label diagnostic is its own result. Cited findings from other papers and the true-label classification results do not test the listed claim versions. The reported random-label result gives no training error.
record.test_reason: The study measures validation performance after scrambling training labels as a selection-bias diagnostic. It reports no random-label training fit, optimization comparison, or learning trajectory. Chance validation MCC alone does not test any listed version, and the diagnostic does not rely on the claimed memorization finding.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report near-zero MCC with random labels, as expected for their selection-bias diagnostic. They do not conclude that networks successfully or unsuccessfully memorize random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The random-label diagnostic uses a DAP with deep features extracted by frozen backend networks and downstream classifiers; it does not test full-network fitting of random labels. The paper describes DAPPER as a validation framework, not a replication of the original random-label experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation MCC ranged close to zero when the DAP was repeated with scrambled training labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scrambling training labels yields chance validation performance in the tested DAPPER diagnostic, consistent with the authors' selection-bias sanity check.

record.peer_reviewed: PLOS Computational Biology, 15(3), as stated in the supplied text.
record.problems: The random-label result is reported only as an aggregate qualitative statement; individual model values, uncertainty, and training error are not stated. The diagnostic uses downstream classifiers on frozen deep features, not the full networks described in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the listed versions. True-label classification results and the reported accuracy improvement from retraining the feature extractor do not test random-label fitting.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero random-label training error under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters; chance validation performance alone does not establish this.
Relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The frozen feature extractor alone is not decisive: a neural classifier head could potentially provide relevant memorization evidence. Here, the absence of a training-fit result prevents that inference.

versions.untested_parts: Whether training error reaches zero or near zero; whether the full deep networks, rather than downstream classifiers on frozen features, fit random labels; and whether the same networks generalize well on true labels.

rows.subject: DAPPER classifier heads (aggregate; individual random-label results not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the DAP after stochastically scrambling training-set labels, then reported MCC.

conditions.value: random labels mode; details not stated

rows.note: The reported MCC is for the random-label diagnostic; the text does not state training error or provide the individual model results. The methods state that MCC = 0 corresponds to random prediction.
rows.check: MCC close to zero concerns predictive validation performance, not training-set memorization. The DAP evaluates downstream classifiers with frozen convolutional feature extractors; individual random-label classifier results and training errors are unspecified. The chance-prediction reference is MCC = 0. The result appears on printed page 12, with the diagnostic described on page 10.

tranche.reason: The random-label experiment diagnoses selection bias through validation MCC; it neither measures random-label training fit nor uses the claimed memorization finding.
